attribution: Traditionally attributed to Shankara; authorship debated
summary: A six-verse hymn, also called Atma Shatakam, in which the speaker negates identification with mind, body, senses and roles, and affirms identity with Shiva as pure consciousness and bliss.
whyRead: In six verses it gives a sung, first-person version of the 'not this, not this' method. It is widely recited and a gentle entry into Advaita's view of the Self.
story: Tradition says the young Shankara composed it when his future teacher Govindapada asked him who he was; this is a traditional account.
questions: Who am I, if not my body, mind or roles?

keyTeachings.title: Negation of the non-Self
keyTeachings.text: Each verse denies that the Self is mind, intellect, ego, senses, elements, breath, merit, demerit, relationships or even the seeker's own practices.

keyTeachings.title: Affirmation
keyTeachings.text: Each verse ends by affirming the Self as consciousness and bliss, named as Shiva, understood here as the non-dual Self.
